reader.decision: Approve removing the per-pod price_cache so get_price reads the database directly. Do not lower the CDN TTL. Before merging, confirm db.fetch_price can handle the load.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the stale price comes from six unsynchronised per-pod caches, not the CDN. Removing the cache fixes the cause and leaves no invalidation logic to fail, whereas pub/sub invalidation can miss messages and leave a pod stale for up to an hour. The one risk is database load, which the message flags but gives no numbers for.

reconstruction.problem: After an admin price change, customers see the old price for up to an hour. The message traces this to the per-pod price_cache in pricing/service.py (TTLCache, ttl=3600) across 6 shop-api replicas. update_price pops the entry only on the pod that handled the admin request. The price.changed event is published, but only search/indexer.py subscribes to it. The CDN rule for /api/* is cache: false, so the CDN is not involved.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Pods B to F keep serving the old price (39.90 instead of 34.90 for KET-2210) for up to 3600 seconds. Reloads return different prices depending on which pod answers, and customers see the old price at checkout until the last pod expires its entry (about 10:58 in the example, matching SM-140).
reconstruction.fix: Delete price_cache and the TTLCache import in pricing/service.py, so get_price returns db.fetch_price(sku) directly. In admin/prices.py, delete the price_cache import and the price_cache.pop(sku, None) line. Make no change to cdn/rules.yaml. The alternatives are to have each pod subscribe to price.changed and pop its own entry, or to set ttl=60 on price_cache.
reconstruction.cost: One database read per price request, and product pages, cart and checkout all call this endpoint. If db.fetch_price is slow under that load, the fix breaks. The subscribe alternative needs a startup hook in shop.app, and a pod that misses a non-durable Redis pub/sub message stays stale for up to an hour. The 60-second TTL is a one-line change but still shows the old price for up to a minute at checkout.

follow_up_questions: What is the current price-read request rate, and what latency does db.fetch_price have under that load? Can the database take every price read?
Can the business accept a stale price for up to 60 seconds at checkout? This only matters if the direct read fails the load check.
reader.closing_answer: Read the database directly in get_price, and remove the per-pod cache. Check db.fetch_price under expected load first. If the database cannot take every price read, fall back to the per-pod price.changed subscription.
